reader.requirement: At --std 85 a format 1 data description entry takes a level-number of 01 through 49 (1 through 9 also written as one digit) or 77 (77 only outside a file record area); 00, 50 through 65, 78 through 99, any three-digit spelling, and 66 or 88 on a format 1 body must be refused.
reader.edition-search: Grepped LevelNumberPass.cs (which also holds LevelNumberRules) for Edition, DialectLevel, Year and Construct, and VersionConformancePass for LevelNumber: no edition test on the path; the pass documents that the level-number sets are the same at every edition, which holds for this rule (§1985:IV.7.4 gives the 1985 set 01-49, 66, 77, 88).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness accepts 01, 02, 05, 10, 49 and 77 in Working-Storage; single-digit spellings, the File Section and the whole refusal half (00, 50, 65, 78, 99, three digits, 66 or 88 on a format 1 body, 77 in an FD) are not exercised

probes.expected: 5, 9 and 09 accepted as single-digit and leading-zero spellings, 9 and 09 the same level
1, 2, 49 and 02 in an FD record, written and read back

probes.printed: error COBOL1746: level-number 77 on 'FX': data description entries subordinate to a FD or SD entry shall have level-numbers ... 66, 88, or 1 through 49
probes.expected: refused: 77 is not a record-area level
refused: 78 is a vendor extension, not a 1985 level-number

probes.printed: error COBOL1746: level-number 100 on 'A': a level-number is expressed as a one-digit or two-digit number
error COBOL1746: level-number 005 on 'A': ... one-digit or two-digit number
probes.expected: refused: only one leading zero form for 1-9

probes.printed: error COBOL1747: level-number 66 on 'A': ... this entry has no RENAMES clause, so it is a format-1 entry, whose level-number may be 77 or 1 through 49
probes.expected: refused: 66 is not a format 1 level

probes.printed: error COBOL1747: level-number 88 on 'A': ... a format-1 entry, whose level-number may be 77 or 1 through 49
probes.expected: refused: 88 is not a format 1 level

probes.printed: error COBOL2771: 'B': level-number 48 is not the level-number 49 of the other items immediately subordinate to the group 'G'
probes.expected: refused by §1985:IV.4.3.2.1 (identical level-numbers for immediate subordinates); 48 itself is in range

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.3.3 SR1  (5.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1
OK  §1985:IV.7.4  (7.4 DATA DIVISION ENTRIES)  the text is in the clause
OK  §1985:IV.4.3.2.1  (4.3.2.1 Level-Numbers)  the text is in the clause

reader.notes: One pass screens every level-number token before binding: the section axis refuses values outside each section's set and the format axis refuses 66 and 88 on a format 1 body; spelling longer than two digits is refused. No edition is consulted, and the 1985 set is the same as the latest edition's for format 1. Messages cite §2023 clauses at --std 85 (wording only).

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: c6_link77 (77-level items in a contained program's Linkage Section, USING, ADD through one) printed 'LW=ABCD / N=008'; c6_77after (77 between two 01 records in Working-Storage) printed 'G=A K=K H=H'; c6_8 (single-digit 8) printed G=A; c6_0 (single-digit 0) refused COBOL1746; c6_077 and c6_049 (three-digit spellings) refused COBOL1746; c6_plus (+5) and c6_dec (5.0) refused COBOL0001; c6_sd77 (77 after an SD record) refused COBOL1746; class c: c6_const (2002 '01 K CONSTANT AS 5') refused COBOL0900 and c6_ls (2002 LOCAL-STORAGE with a 77) refused COBOL0900. Cite: OK §1985:VI.5.3.3 SR1 'Level-number in format 1 may be any number from 01 through 49 or 77'.
